You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station T-22, survey area T. Interpreted layer model:

4 | 3433.8 | 1.21 | 10.55

6 | 9531.9 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as AAKH-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station T-22, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

Station T-22, located in survey area T, consists of a six-layer subsurface profile. The resistivity values for these layers are 177.3, 706.0, 3320.1, 3433.8, 794.3, and 9531.9 ohm-m. By analyzing the consecutive triplets of resistivity values, we determine the following transitions: an increasing sequence for layers 1-2-3 (A), an increasing sequence for layers 2-3-4 (A), a maximum for layers 3-4-5 (K), and a minimum for layers 4-5-6 (H). Consequently, the derived curve type is AAKH. This result is consistent with the classification currently recorded on file.
